newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen mostly steady-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen mostly steady-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt, amid continued strength from light hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $51.00 to $51.50 and Illinois top prices at the plant could range $50.00 to $50.50.

Prices in Illinois and Iowa could also be underpinned by weather, with heavy rains in Illinois spurring flood concerns and possiblity of traffic disruptions on country roads. Snow in southeastern Iowa also could limit hog movement, they said.
Snowfall outlooks were varied, with expected amounts seen from two to three inches in central Illinois and seven inches or more in southeastern Iowa, local dealers said.
Light support also was expected from firm pork prices, they said.
Fresh pork loins prices were not fully established, hams weighing 20-26 lbs were $2.00 per cwt higher, bellies generally steady and lean trimmings $2.00 higher, USDA said.
There were 27.0 loads of pork cuts and 33.0 loads of trimmed/processed pork sold, USDA said.
